# Introduction

The Collaborative Institutional Training Initiative (CITI) Program provides training on research ethics, responsible research practices, and the protection of human subjects.

As part of the Cal Poly Pomona research requirements, I completed the College of Business Administration CITI training, which focuses on ethical considerations when conducting research involving human participants.

This report documents the training requirements and provides evidence of completion through the CITI training certificate.

# CITI Training Overview

The CITI training introduces important principles related to conducting ethical research and protecting research participants.

The College of Business Administration training includes topics such as:

- Introduction to human subjects research
- Ethical principles and research responsibilities
- Protection of research participants
- Informed consent and confidentiality
- Data collection in other countries
- Online research and data collection

These topics are relevant to marketing research because researchers must ensure that participants are treated ethically and that their personal information is protected.

# Conclusion

Completing the CITI training provides a foundation for understanding ethical practices when conducting research involving human subjects.

The training emphasizes the importance of informed consent, participant confidentiality, and responsible data collection.

These principles are essential when conducting marketing research, particularly when collecting survey responses and analyzing consumer information.
